configs.kafka_compose:
# Apache Kafka for the head-to-head comparison (#595, #596): three brokers in
# KRaft mode, each a combined broker+controller, RF=3, min.insync.replicas=2.
#
# Fairness rule 1: every broker gets EXACTLY the limits each VTOP node gets in
# compose.vtop.yml (2 CPUs, 2 GiB, no swap, a named volume on the same Docker
# VM disk). Change one file, change the other; run.py records both in
# environment.json and refuses to start when they differ.
#
# Everything else is Kafka as shipped (profile `defaults`, #595 rule 4): no
# flush.messages, so a broker acknowledges on replication, not on fsync.
#
# The image is pinned by tag AND digest (rule 8); KAFKA_IMAGE overrides both.
name: kc-kafka

x-broker: &broker
  image: ${KAFKA_IMAGE:-apache/kafka:4.3.2@sha256:852a0d49fc4e656b022e7f23785411802c9a088c78a7c5e39f33969de9c227a7}
  cpus: 2
  mem_limit: 2g
  memswap_limit: 2g
  ulimits:
    nofile: { soft: 65536, hard: 65536 }
  networks: [bench]
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD-SHELL", "/opt/kafka/bin/kafka-broker-api-versions.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 > /dev/null 2>&1"]
    interval: 5s
    timeout: 20s
    retries: 30
    start_period: 10s

x-env: &env
  # One fixed id: KRaft formats every log dir with it on first start.
  CLUSTER_ID: "a2NvbXBhcmUtcGhhc2UtMQ"
  KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: "broker,controller"
  KAFKA_LISTENERS: "PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093"
  KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: "CONTROLLER"
  KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME: "PLAINTEXT"
  KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: "CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT"
  KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: "1@kafka-1:9093,2@kafka-2:9093,3@kafka-3:9093"
  KAFKA_LOG_DIRS: "/var/lib/kafka/data"
  # The replication contract (#595 rule 3).
  KAFKA_DEFAULT_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "3"
  KAFKA_MIN_INSYNC_REPLICAS: "2"
  KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "3"
  KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "3"
  KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: "2"
  # The benchmark topic is created explicitly by run.py with these settings;
  # a typo'd topic must not be auto-created with others.
  KAFKA_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE: "false"

services:
  kafka-1:
    <<: *broker
    hostname: kafka-1
    environment:
      <<: *env
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: "1"
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: "PLAINTEXT://kafka-1:9092"
    volumes: ["kafka-1-data:/var/lib/kafka/data"]
  kafka-2:
    <<: *broker
    hostname: kafka-2
    environment:
      <<: *env
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: "2"
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: "PLAINTEXT://kafka-2:9092"
    volumes: ["kafka-2-data:/var/lib/kafka/data"]
  kafka-3:
    <<: *broker
    hostname: kafka-3
    environment:
      <<: *env
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: "3"
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: "PLAINTEXT://kafka-3:9092"
    volumes: ["kafka-3-data:/var/lib/kafka/data"]

volumes:
  kafka-1-data:
  kafka-2-data:
  kafka-3-data:

networks:
  bench:
    name: kc-kafka-bench
configs.vtop_compose:
# VTOP for the failover comparison (#597): three co-located nodes, each a
# metadata Raft voter plus a CANDIDATE replica of the one range (configs in
# vtop/ha-node-*.yaml), the Helm chart's replicated shape. Leadership follows
# the metadata lease, so killing the leader is a failover, not a stop.
#
# Fairness rule 1: EXACTLY the per-node limits compose.kafka.yml gives each
# Kafka broker (2 CPUs, 2 GiB, no swap, a named volume on the same Docker VM
# disk); failover.py refuses to start when they differ, as run.py does.
#
# VTOP_IMAGE is the image failover.py built from the commit under test;
# VTOP_TLS_DIR is the per-run certificate directory it minted (never
# committed). No healthcheck gates `up`: a co-located node is ready only once
# its metadata group is initialised, which failover.py does after `up`.
name: kc-vtop-ha

x-node: &node
  image: ${VTOP_IMAGE:?set VTOP_IMAGE to the vtop-bench image failover.py built}
  entrypoint: ["vtop-node", "node", "--config", "/etc/vtop/node.yaml"]
  cpus: 2
  mem_limit: 2g
  memswap_limit: 2g
  ulimits:
    nofile: { soft: 65536, hard: 65536 }
  networks: [bench]

services:
  vtop-1:
    <<: *node
    hostname: vtop-1
    volumes:
      - "./vtop/ha-node-1.yaml:/etc/vtop/node.yaml:ro"
      - "${VTOP_TLS_DIR:?set VTOP_TLS_DIR to the minted certificate directory}:/etc/vtop/tls:ro"
      - "vtop-1-data:/home/vtop"
  vtop-2:
    <<: *node
    hostname: vtop-2
    volumes:
      - "./vtop/ha-node-2.yaml:/etc/vtop/node.yaml:ro"
      - "${VTOP_TLS_DIR:?set VTOP_TLS_DIR to the minted certificate directory}:/etc/vtop/tls:ro"
      - "vtop-2-data:/home/vtop"
  vtop-3:
    <<: *node
    hostname: vtop-3
    volumes:
      - "./vtop/ha-node-3.yaml:/etc/vtop/node.yaml:ro"
      - "${VTOP_TLS_DIR:?set VTOP_TLS_DIR to the minted certificate directory}:/etc/vtop/tls:ro"
      - "vtop-3-data:/home/vtop"

volumes:
  vtop-1-data:
  vtop-2-data:
  vtop-3-data:

networks:
  bench:
    name: kc-vtop-ha-bench
configs.vtop_driver:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The VTOP native-path client for the failover benchmark (#597), run by
# failover.py inside a container of the vtop-bench image on the cluster's
# network. It is what a Kafka client does for itself and the native client
# does not: find the leader, produce to it, and when the produce ends early
# (connection lost, refused, or no answer within the request timeout), look
# the leader up again and resume from the acknowledged floor.
#
# NOT the Kafka client path: a candidate node refuses the Kafka gateway, so no
# Kafka client can follow a VTOP failover (see docs/benchmarks/kafka-failover.md).
#
# Behaviour kept comparable with the JVM producer on the Kafka side:
#   - one fixed-rate schedule for the whole run (`--rate` anchored at
#     ANCHOR_US), so records the outage delayed are sent as a backlog after
#     it, as the JVM producer sends what it buffered;
#   - the leader is looked up again only when a produce ends, never on a
#     timer: the JVM client also refreshes metadata on an error or a request
#     timeout, not by watching the controller;
#   - REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS is the JVM client's request.timeout.ms default and
#     BACKOFF_SECONDS its retry.backoff.ms default;
#   - one producer identity and epoch for the whole run, resumed with
#     `--first-sequence <acked floor>`: a batch that was written but whose
#     acknowledgement was lost is answered from the broker's deduplication
#     state rather than written twice (the JVM side is idempotent too).
#
# Separately, a lease observer polls metadata every LEASE_POLL_SECONDS and
# logs each change of holder or epoch; it feeds only the "time to new
# leader" measurement, never the producer.
#
# Writes under /out: acks.log (one line per acknowledged batch, from
# `vtop-node produce --ack-log`), acked (the floor), driver.log and lease.log
# (`<unix_micros> <event...>`), done (when TOTAL records are acknowledged).
set -u

: "${TOTAL:?}" "${RATE:?}" "${BATCH:?}" "${VALUE_BYTES:?}" "${ANCHOR_US:?}"
REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS="${REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS:-30000}"
BACKOFF_SECONDS="${BACKOFF_SECONDS:-0.1}"
LEASE_POLL_SECONDS="${LEASE_POLL_SECONDS:-0.1}"
TOPIC_UUID="aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000b1"
RANGE_UUID="aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000c1"
OUT=/out

now_us() { local t="$EPOCHREALTIME"; echo "${t/./}"; }
note() { echo "$(now_us) $*" >> "$OUT/driver.log"; }

# The admin configs, one per metadata voter, written by failover.py. A read is
# tried at each in turn, each bounded, so a dead or cut-off voter costs at
# most its bound and never wedges the loop.
#
# Parsed with bash alone: the runtime image has perl-base, without JSON::PP.
# `lease` is a flat object, so its fields are read from inside its braces.
read_lease() {
  local n json lease holder epoch
  for n in 1 2 3; do
    if json="$(timeout 2 vtopctl --json meta range-lease --config "$OUT/admin-$n.yaml" \
      --topic-uuid "$TOPIC_UUID" --range-uuid "$RANGE_UUID" 2>/dev/null)"; then
      json="${json//[$'\n\t ']/}"
      [[ "$json" =~ \"lease\":\{([^}]*)\} ]] || continue
      lease="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
      [[ "$lease" =~ \"holder_node_uuid\":\"([0-9a-f-]+)\" ]] || continue
      holder="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
      [[ "$lease" =~ \"fencing_epoch\":([0-9]+) ]] || continue
      epoch="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
      echo "$holder $epoch"
      return 0
    fi
  done
  return 1
}

observe_lease() {
  local last="" current
  while [[ ! -e "$OUT/done" ]]; do
    if current="$(read_lease)"; then
      if [[ "$current" != "$last" ]]; then
        echo "$(now_us) $current" >> "$OUT/lease.log"
        last="$current"
      fi
    else
      echo "$(now_us) unreadable" >> "$OUT/lease.log"
    fi
    sleep "$LEASE_POLL_SECONDS"
  done
}

client_config() { # <epoch>
  local path="$OUT/client-$1.yaml"
  cat > "$path" <<EOF
cluster_id: 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555
principal_id: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ce
producer_id: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ce
producer_epoch: 1
fencing_epoch: $1
range: { topic: "bench", topic_epoch: 1, range_id: $RANGE_UUID, range_generation: 0 }
server_name: "localhost"
tls: { ca: /etc/vtop/tls/ca.pem, cert: /etc/vtop/tls/data-1.pem, key: /etc/vtop/tls/data-1-key.pem }
EOF
  echo "$path"
}

observe_lease &
OBSERVER=$!

acked=0
attempt=0
note "start total=$TOTAL rate=$RATE batch=$BATCH request_timeout_ms=$REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS"
while [[ "$acked" -lt "$TOTAL" ]]; do
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  if ! lease="$(read_lease)"; then
    note "attempt=$attempt lease_unreadable"
    sleep "$BACKOFF_SECONDS"
    continue
  fi
  read -r holder epoch <<<"$lease"
  # The node uuids end in a1..a3 and the containers are vtop-1..3.
  node="${holder: -1}"
  config="$(client_config "$epoch")"
  note "attempt=$attempt produce holder=$holder epoch=$epoch addr=vtop-$node:9400 first=$acked"
  vtop-node produce --client-config "$config" --addr "vtop-$node:9400" \
    --records "$((TOTAL - acked))" --first-sequence "$acked" --batch "$BATCH" \
    --value-bytes "$VALUE_BYTES" --durability quorum --acked-file "$OUT/acked" \
    --rate "$RATE" --rate-anchor-unix-micros "$ANCHOR_US" --ack-log "$OUT/acks.log" \
    --request-timeout-ms "$REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS" > "$OUT/produce.out" 2> "$OUT/produce.err"
  code=$?
  acked="$(cat "$OUT/acked" 2>/dev/null || echo "$acked")"
  reason="$(tail -c 300 "$OUT/produce.err" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  note "attempt=$attempt exit=$code acked=$acked reason=$reason"
  if [[ "$code" -ne 0 ]]; then
    sleep "$BACKOFF_SECONDS"
  fi
done
note "done acked=$acked attempts=$attempt"
touch "$OUT/done"
wait "$OBSERVER"
configs.vtop_node_1:
# VTOP node 1 for the failover comparison (#597): a CO-LOCATED node, one
# process hosting a metadata Raft voter and a CANDIDATE replica of the one
# range, the shape the Helm chart renders for a replicated topology (#284,
# #287). The three members are identical apart from identity; whichever
# acquires the range lease leads, and when it dies a survivor takes the range
# in place, with no restart and no config rewritten.
#
# The counterpart of Kafka's combined broker+controller nodes in
# compose.kafka.yml: three containers, each a voter of the metadata quorum and
# a replica of the partition.
#
# Promotion fences the other replicas over the replica plane, and the node
# refuses that on a plaintext plane, so every plane here is TLS (the phase-1
# static leader ran plaintext and could not fail over at all). failover.py
# mints the certificates per run with scripts/live-chaos/gen-certs.sh (SAN
# localhost, hence server_name "localhost"); none is committed.
#
# No `kafka` block: the node refuses one on a candidate (see the failover
# report). Every timing knob not written here is the binary's default (profile
# `defaults`, #595 rule 5): lease 15 s, renew 5 s, poll 2 s; Raft election
# 300-600 ms, heartbeat 60 ms; segment format v1.
meta:
  node_id: 1
  cluster_id: 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555
  data_dir: /home/vtop/meta
  peer_listen: "0.0.0.0:9100"
  admin_listen: "0.0.0.0:9200"
  # The full voter set, identical on every node; the binary ignores its own.
  peers:
    - { id: 1, addr: "vtop-1:9100", server_name: "localhost" }
    - { id: 2, addr: "vtop-2:9100", server_name: "localhost" }
    - { id: 3, addr: "vtop-3:9100", server_name: "localhost" }
  tls: { ca: /etc/vtop/tls/ca.pem, cert: /etc/vtop/tls/meta-1.pem, key: /etc/vtop/tls/meta-1-key.pem }
data:
  role: candidate
  # The same list on every member, this node included; the binary skips its own.
  peers:
    - { node_uuid: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1, addr: "vtop-1:9300", server_name: "localhost" }
    - { node_uuid: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a2, addr: "vtop-2:9300", server_name: "localhost" }
    - { node_uuid: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a3, addr: "vtop-3:9300", server_name: "localhost" }
  node_uuid: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1
  cluster_id: 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555
  data_dir: /home/vtop/data
  # The floor of the epoch view, not an epoch to serve at: grants are minted from 1.
  fencing_epoch: 0
  range: { topic: "bench", topic_epoch: 1, range_id: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000c1, range_generation: 0 }
  segment_id: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000d1
  native_listen: "0.0.0.0:9400"
  replica_listen: "0.0.0.0:9300"
  replica_tls: { ca: /etc/vtop/tls/ca.pem, cert: /etc/vtop/tls/data-1.pem, key: /etc/vtop/tls/data-1-key.pem }
  native_tls: { ca: /etc/vtop/tls/ca.pem, cert: /etc/vtop/tls/data-1.pem, key: /etc/vtop/tls/data-1-key.pem }
  principal_id: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ce
  lease:
    # Ask this process's own metadata voter first; admin_peers is where a
    # redirect to the Raft leader leads (#292).
    admin_endpoint: "127.0.0.1:9200"
    server_name: "localhost"
    topic_uuid: aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-0000000000b1
    tls: { ca: /etc/vtop/tls/ca.pem, cert: /etc/vtop/tls/data-1.pem, key: /etc/vtop/tls/data-1-key.pem }
    admin_peers:
      - { node_id: 1, endpoint: "vtop-1:9200", server_name: "localhost" }
      - { node_id: 2, endpoint: "vtop-2:9200", server_name: "localhost" }
      - { node_id: 3, endpoint: "vtop-3:9200", server_name: "localhost" }
observability: { listen: "0.0.0.0:9600" }
